_comment: Tokens per agent x model x step. This view is where the design's per-step correctness actually lives, so all three binding join rules are encoded in the SQL rather than described in prose.
name: tokens-per-step
title: Tokens per agent, model and step
description: Token usage attributed to the step that spent it, broken down by agent and model. A step's own row excludes anything a quality gate spent inside it; that spend is shown in Spend outside steps instead. Rows ending in '-tail' are the work a step's closing turn finished after the step formally ended, which belongs to the step that caused it.
af_decision_o4: O-4 (view delivery) is hybrid: files on disk plus a best-effort dashboard push. See README.md.
af_assumptions: VERIFIED AGAINST A LIVE BACKEND, AND ONLY IN PART — read this with entry 1. During review of PR #567 OpenObserve v0.91.3 was stood up from the pinned artifact, both planes were ingested, and THIS view's query was run verbatim — it reproduced the token totals derived by hand from the acceptance criteria, column spelling for column spelling. install_telemetry_views/README.md states, in the same paragraph as that verification, that 'the native event shape remains the synthetic fixture's hypothesis until a real capture replaces it'. It does not say in so many words what was ingested on the native side; that it was the synthetic fixture (internal/telemetry/testdata/synthetic/api_request_events.json) is an INFERENCE from that sentence, and it is the only reading that explains how a run against a real backend could have confirmed the column spellings while leaving the shape hypothetical. So that run confirms the TRACES-side spellings and the join rules against a real backend, and confirms nothing about the native event shape beyond the hypothesis it was given. GOVERNS: PR #567 governs the traces-side spellings and the three join rules. The capture in internal/telemetry/testdata/openobserve-v0.91.3/ governs the native event shape, and it disagrees: tokens_search_response_query_failed.json records this query returning HTTP 400 code 20004, 'No field named af_overhead', with the logs stream admitting only _timestamp, af_agent, af_formula_instance and service_name — while 2,192 records for one agent sit in that same stream (tokens_search_response_ok.json) and the metrics plane carries claude_code_token_usage for the same runs (metrics_promql_response.json). The native plane reached that host; the token-bearing COLUMNS this query reads did not. UNRESOLVED: why those columns are absent for Claude Code 2.1.220 on that host is not established here, and this view is not re-authored on the strength of one capture. The metrics plane is not the answer to it either: its label set carries no step attribute of any kind, so reading token totals from there would silently turn a per-step table into per-run totals. Until a recorded-real native capture defines the columns, treat the per-step token table as unverified against real Claude Code output and read the whole-run figures from the metrics plane instead. CI still has no backend, so none of this is re-verified automatically. That live run observed af_step_seq as a string; the ordering key is now cast to an integer here, and the encoder emits it as an integer, so ordering is correct under either ingest typing. A dashboard already published under this title is never replaced by a re-run of quickstart.sh, so an existing factory keeps the query it first received — re-import this file by hand to pick up changes.

The native claude_code.api_request shape (input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd) is the synthetic fixture's hypothesis, not a recorded capture - see internal/telemetry/testdata/synthetic/api_request_events.json, which P6b replaces. Whether these arrive as OTel logs or metrics is also an inference; if it is metrics, the stream name and column prefix both change. The capture in internal/telemetry/testdata/openobserve-v0.91.3/ is the first real observation of this plane and it does NOT confirm the hypothesis: see entry 0 for which observation governs which half.

Attribute names are rewritten on ingest. Trace resource attributes are prefixed with 'service_' and every dot becomes an underscore, so af.formula_instance is queryable only as service_af_formula_instance. OTLP logs do NOT get the prefix, so the same attribute is af_formula_instance on the native-event side of the join. _timestamp is microseconds while start_time/end_time are nanoseconds and duration is microseconds.
Native events carry no per-request id, so an event is identified for de-duplication by (formula run, agent, timestamp). Two requests from one agent in the same microsecond would collapse.

queries.query:
WITH step_windows AS (
    -- Rule 2, earliest start wins. The af side has already applied earliest-wins when it computed
    -- each step's duration, and only closed steps are exported, so in practice this aggregates one
    -- row per step. MIN/MAX are kept because the rule must survive a second span for the same step
    -- arriving later - a wide window is visible in the reconciliation view, a narrow one is not.
    SELECT service_af_formula_instance AS formula_run,
           af_step_id                  AS step,
           service_af_agent            AS agent,
           max(CAST(af_step_seq AS BIGINT)) AS step_order,
           max(af_model)               AS model,
           min(start_time)             AS window_start_ns,
           max(end_time)               AS window_end_ns
    FROM "traces"."default"
    WHERE service_name = 'agentfactory'
      AND af_step_id <> ''
    GROUP BY service_af_formula_instance, af_step_id, service_af_agent
),
billable_requests AS (
    -- Rule 1, overhead exclusion: an event carrying af.overhead belongs to its overhead bucket and
    -- to NO step, even when it fired mid-step. Without this a quality gate running inside a step is
    -- counted into that step's "exact" cost and the reconciliation view still balances, so the only
    -- symptom is a step that looks more expensive than the work it did. An EMPTY marker is not a
    -- marker, matching AttributeEvent, which requires a non-empty bucket name.
    SELECT af_formula_instance AS formula_run,
           af_agent            AS agent,
           _timestamp * 1000   AS at_ns,
           input_tokens,
           output_tokens
    FROM "logs"."default"
    WHERE af_overhead IS NULL OR af_overhead = ''
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT e.formula_run,
           e.agent,
           w.step,
           w.step_order,
           w.model,
           e.input_tokens,
           e.output_tokens,
           CASE WHEN e.at_ns < w.window_end_ns THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS is_tail,
           row_number() OVER (
               PARTITION BY e.formula_run, e.agent, e.at_ns
               -- A window that contains the event wins outright. Among containing windows the
               -- earliest start wins, matching AttributeEvent, which returns the first container in
               -- start order. Otherwise the tail goes to the window with the greatest end at or
               -- before the event, which is also what AttributeEvent does.
               ORDER BY CASE WHEN e.at_ns < w.window_end_ns THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
                        CASE WHEN e.at_ns < w.window_end_ns THEN w.window_start_ns END ASC,
                        w.window_end_ns DESC
           ) AS pick
    FROM billable_requests e
    JOIN step_windows w
      -- Instance AND agent scoping are explicit. AttributeEvent omits both because its caller
      -- supplies one agent's records at a time; SQL over a shared stream has no such caller, and
      -- without these predicates one agent's events attribute to another agent's steps.
      ON w.formula_run = e.formula_run
     AND w.agent       = e.agent
     -- Rule 3a, half-open window: the start instant belongs to the step.
     AND e.at_ns >= w.window_start_ns
)
SELECT formula_run,
       agent,
       model,
       -- Rule 3b, directional boundary: spend after step_end and before the next step_start is
       -- attributed BACKWARDS to the step that caused it, as a distinguishable '-tail' component.
       -- The closing turn keeps working after af done returns, so this tail is predictable rather
       -- than symmetric noise, and folding it forwards would show phantom cost between steps.
       CASE WHEN is_tail = 1 THEN step || '-tail' ELSE step END AS step_bucket,
       min(step_order)                   AS step_order,
       count(*)                          AS requests,
       sum(input_tokens)                 AS input_tokens,
       sum(output_tokens)                AS output_tokens,
       sum(input_tokens + output_tokens) AS total_tokens
FROM ranked
WHERE pick = 1
GROUP BY formula_run, agent, model,
         CASE WHEN is_tail = 1 THEN step || '-tail' ELSE step END
ORDER BY formula_run, step_order, step_bucket
